translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way.”
“A voice cries out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
John appeared in the wilderness, baptizing and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole region of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and he was baptizing them in the Jordan as they confessed their sins.
John himself wore clothing made of camel hair, with a leather belt tied around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, “Look, someone more powerful than I am is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the straps of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
As soon as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you.”
Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
He was there in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and angels were serving him.
After John was handed over, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God
and saying, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has arrived. Repent and believe the good news.”
As he was walking along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
When he had gone a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and his brother John. They too were in a boat, mending their nets.
He called them, and immediately they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and followed him.
When they entered Capernaum, he immediately began teaching in their synagogues on the Sabbaths.
They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as someone with authority, not like their scribes.
In their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out
and said, “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked him and said, “Shut your mouth and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit threw him down, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
They were all amazed and began asking one another, “What is this? What is this new teaching? With authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
Immediately the news about him spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
They left the synagogue and came to the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Simon's mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and they told him about her.
He went over, took her by the hand, and raised her up. Immediately her fever left her, and she began serving them.
In the evening, at sunset, they brought him everyone who was sick and those possessed by demons.
The whole town was gathered at the door.
He healed many who were suffering from various diseases and drove out many demons. He would not let the demons speak, because they knew him.
Very early in the morning he got up and went to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
Simon and those with him were searching for him.
When they found him, they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
He said to them, “Go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there too, because this is why I came.”
He preached in all their synagogues throughout Galilee and drove out demons.
A man with leprosy came to him and fell at his feet. He begged him, saying, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus had compassion on him, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be cleansed.”
At that very moment his leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.
He sternly warned him and sent him away,
and said to him, “See that you tell no one. Instead, go, show yourself to the priests, and offer the sacrifice for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

But when he went out, he began proclaiming it widely and spreading the news, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly. Instead, he stayed outside in a deserted place, and people came to him from everywhere.
After some days Jesus entered Capernaum again. When they heard that he was in the house,
many gathered, so that there was no room to hold them, not even in front of the door. He was speaking the word to them.
They came to him, bringing him a paralyzed man carried by four people.

Since they could not get near him because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and removed the roofing above the place where Jesus was. Then they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man was lying.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “My son, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes and Pharisees were sitting there, thinking in their hearts,
“Why is this man speaking blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
But Jesus knew in his spirit that they were thinking these things within themselves, and he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—
“I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
Immediately he got up, picked up his mat, and went out in front of them all. They were all amazed and praised God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
He went out again to the sea. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Come, follow me.” He got up and followed him.
While he was reclining at a meal in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many of them, and they had followed him.
When the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but those who are very sick do. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to him, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but your own disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? No.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them. Then they will fast on that day.
No one puts a new patch on an old garment and sews it on. Otherwise, the new patch pulls away from the old garment, and the tear becomes worse.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the wine bursts the skins, the skins are ruined, and the wine spills out. Instead, they put new wine into new wineskins.”
As Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, his disciples walked along, picking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”
Jesus said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he and those with him were in need and hungry?
How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread from the Lord’s table, which only the priests are permitted to eat, and also gave some to those who were with him?
He said to them, “The Sabbath was created for human beings, not human beings for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
Jesus entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They were watching him to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
He said to the man whose hand was withered, “Stand up in the middle.”
He also said to them, “Is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent.
He looked at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees immediately went out and took counsel with Herod’s supporters against him, planning how to destroy him.
Jesus went away to the sea with his disciples. A large crowd from Galilee followed him, and from Judea.
And from Jerusalem, from Edom, from beyond the Jordan, from Tyre, and from Sidon, great crowds who had heard everything he was doing came to him.
He told his disciples to have a boat ready for him because of the crowds, so that they would not crush him.
For he was healing many, so that they were pressing upon him to touch him.
And those who had afflictions from unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, would fall down and cry out, saying, “You are the Son of God!”
He sternly warned them not to reveal who he was.
He went up the mountain and called those he wanted, and they came to him.
He chose twelve to be with him and to send them out to preach,
and to have authority to heal the sick and drive out demons.
He gave Simon the name Cephas.
And to James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James he gave the name Boanerges, which means “sons of thunder.”
And Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot,
and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him. And they came to a house.
The crowds gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
His relatives heard about it and went out to seize him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebub in him,” and, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
Jesus called them over and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
For if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand; instead, his end has come.
No one can enter a strong man’s house and seize his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven all their sins and whatever blasphemies they utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness, but is liable to eternal judgment.”
This was because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit in him.”
His mother and his brothers came and stood outside, and they sent word to call him to them.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
He answered them, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
He looked at those sitting beside him and said, “Here is my mother, and here are my brothers.”
“For whoever does the will of God is my brother and my sister and my mother.”
Again he began teaching beside the sea. Large crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat on the sea and sat down. The whole crowd stood on the land beside the sea.
He taught them much through parables, and in his teaching he said:
“Listen! A sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some seed fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate it.
Other seed fell on rock, where there was not much soil. It sprouted immediately because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it dried up.
Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no fruit.
Other seed fell on good soil, sprouted, grew, and produced a crop: some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, and some a hundredfold.”
He said, “Whoever has ears to hear should listen.”
When they were alone, those who were with him, together with his twelve, asked him about that parable.
Jesus said to them, “You have been given knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom of God. But for those outside, everything is in parables,
so that they may look and look but not see, and listen and listen but not understand, lest they turn back and their sins be forgiven them.”
He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How, then, will you understand all the parables?
The sower who sowed was sowing the word.
Those beside the road are the ones in whom the word is sown. When they hear it, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown in their hearts.
Those sown on rock are the ones who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy.
But they have no root in themselves and last only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
Those sown among thorns are the ones who have heard the word,
but the worries of this world, the deception of wealth, and all the other desires enter and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Those sown in good soil are the ones who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”
He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a measuring basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing kept secret that will not come to light.
If anyone has ears to hear, let them listen.”
And he said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured out to you, and more will be added to you who listen.
For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”
And he said, “The kingdom of God is like this: like a man who scatters seed on the ground,
and sleeps and rises, night and day, while the seed grows and becomes tall, without his knowing how.
For the earth produces the crop: first the stalk, then the head, and finally the fully developed grain in the head.
But when the crop ripens, the sickle comes immediately, because the harvest has arrived.”
And he said, “To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, and with what parable shall we illustrate it?
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on earth.
But when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and produces large branches, so that birds can dwell in its shade.”
Jesus spoke to them in parables like these, according to what they were able to understand.
He did not speak to them without parables, but privately, when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything to them.
That day, in the evening, he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side.”
They left the crowds and took him along, just as he was in the boat. Other boats were with them.
A great storm with strong wind arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that it was nearly full.
But Jesus was asleep on a cushion at the back of the boat. They came and woke him, saying to him, “Our teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
He rose, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be quiet! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, “Why are you so afraid? And why do you have no faith?”
They were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who, then, is this, that the winds and the sea obey him?”
He came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gadarenes.
When he got out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came from among the tombs and met him.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him, even with chains.
For whenever he was bound with shackles and chains, he would break the chains and snap the shackles, and no one could subdue him.
Constantly, night and day, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
He cried out in a loud voice and said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”
For he had been saying to him, “Come out of the man, unclean spirit!”
He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “Our name is Legion, because we are many.”
He begged him earnestly not to send him out of the region.
Now a large herd of pigs was grazing there near the mountain.
Those demons begged him, saying, “Send us into those pigs, so that we may enter them.”
He gave them permission. Those unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs. The herd rushed toward the cliff and fell into the sea, about two thousand of them, and they drowned in the water.
Those who were tending them ran away and reported it in the town and also in the villages. People went out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had Legion in him—and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man who had been possessed by demons, and also about the pigs.
They began begging him to leave their territory.
As he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged him to let him stay with him.
He did not let him, but said to him, “Go home to your own people and tell them what the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.”
He went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis what Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.
When Jesus crossed over in the boat to the other side, large crowds gathered around him again while he was beside the sea.
One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw him, he fell at his feet.
He begged him earnestly, saying to him, “My daughter is very ill. Come and lay your hand on her, so that she may get well and live.”
Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed him closely and pressed against him.
Now there was a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years,
who had suffered greatly under many doctors and had spent everything she had, but had not been helped at all. Instead, she had grown even worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the press of the crowd and touched his clothing.
For she had been saying, “If I touch even his clothes, I will be healed.”
Immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she felt in her body that she had been healed of her affliction.
Jesus immediately knew within himself that power had gone out from him. He turned toward the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said to him, “You see the crowds pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
He was looking around to see who had done this.
But the woman, frightened and trembling because she knew what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, “My daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace, and be well, free from your affliction.”
While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s house and said, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?”
But Jesus heard what they said and told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid. Only believe.”
He did not allow anyone to go with him except Simon Peter, James, and John, James’s brother.
They came to the synagogue leader’s house, and he saw people in an uproar, weeping and wailing.
He went in and said to them, “Why are you making an uproar and weeping? The girl has not died but is asleep.”
They laughed at him. But he put them all outside, took the girl’s father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the girl was lying.
He took the girl by the hand and said to her, “Girl, get up.”
Immediately the girl got up and began walking, for she was twelve years old. They were utterly amazed.
He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
He left there and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

When the Sabbath came, he began teaching in the synagogue. Many who heard him were amazed and said, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, that miracles like these happen through his hands?”
“Is this not the carpenter, Mary’s son and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not dishonored except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household.”
He could not perform even one miracle there, except that he laid his hand on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed at their lack of faith. And he went around the villages, teaching.
He called his twelve and began sending them out two by two. He gave them authority over unclean spirits to drive them out.
He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their purses.
They were to wear sandals, but not to wear two tunics.
He said to them, “Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place.

If any people will not welcome you or listen to you, when you leave there, shake off the dust beneath your feet as a testimony against them. Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.”
They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
They drove out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.
King Herod heard about Jesus, for his name had become known to him. He said, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead. That is why miracles are being performed through him.”
Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent men to arrest John and had bound him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to marry your brother’s wife.”
But Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. He listened to him about many things and acted on them, and he enjoyed listening to him.
A special day came when Herod, on his birthday, held a dinner for his nobles, his military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
Herodias's daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those dining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
He swore to her, “Whatever you ask, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask him for?” She said to her, “The head of John the Baptist.”
Immediately she hurried in to the king and said to him, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter right now.”
The king was deeply distressed, but because of his oaths and those dining with him, he did not want to refuse her.
Instead, the king immediately sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John's head. He went and cut off John's head in prison.
He brought it on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
When his disciples heard, they came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and everything they had taught.
He said to them, “Come, let us go off by ourselves into the wilderness, and rest a little.” For many people were coming and going, and they had no opportunity even to eat.
They went away by themselves in a boat to a deserted place.
Many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran overland from all the towns and arrived there ahead of him.
When Jesus came out, he saw large crowds and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began to teach them many things.
When it had grown late, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and it is already late.
Send them away so that they can go to the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?”
He said to them, “Go and see how many loaves you have here.” When they had checked, they said to him, “Five loaves and two fish.”
He instructed them to have everyone sit down in groups on the grass.
They sat down in groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.

He took those five loaves and the two fish and looked up to heaven. He blessed and broke the bread and gave it to his disciples to set before the people. They also divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
They gathered twelve baskets full of broken pieces, including pieces of the fish.
Those who ate the bread were five thousand men.
Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he dismissed the crowds.
After dismissing them, he went to the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on land.
He saw them struggling as they rowed, because the wind was against them. During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came toward them, walking on the water, and he intended to pass them by.
But when they saw him walking on the water, they thought he was a phantom and cried out.
For they all saw him and were afraid. Immediately he spoke with them and said to them, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. They were utterly amazed and astonished within themselves.
For they had not understood from that bread, because their hearts were hardened.
When they had crossed to the other side, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
When they got out of the boat, the local people immediately recognized him.
They ran throughout that whole region and began bringing those who were sick, carrying them on beds to wherever they heard he was.
Wherever he entered villages or towns, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his clothing. Everyone who touched him was healed.
The Pharisees and scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
They saw some of his disciples eating bread without having washed their hands, and they found fault.
For all the Jews and the Pharisees do not eat unless they have carefully washed their hands, because they hold to the tradition of the elders.
After returning from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they bathe. There are also many other practices they have received and observe: the washing of cups, pitchers, copper vessels, and beds.
The scribes and Pharisees asked him, “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread without having washed their hands?”
He said to them, “The prophet Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments as doctrines.’
For you have abandoned the commandment of God and hold to human tradition: the washing of cups and pitchers, and many other things like these.”
He said to them, “You do a fine job of rejecting the commandment of God in order to uphold your tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever curses father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever benefit you might receive from me is my offering,’
you do not allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
You reject the word of God because of the tradition you have handed down. And you do many things like these.”
Jesus called the whole crowd and said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that can defile them by entering them. Rather, what comes out of a person is what defiles them.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
When Jesus left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about that parable.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not know that nothing entering a person from outside can defile them?
For it does not enter their heart but their stomach, and it is expelled into the latrine, which clears away all the food.”
“But what comes out of a person is what defiles that person.
For from within, from people's hearts, come evil thoughts, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, murder,
greed, wickedness, deceit, indecency, envy, blasphemy, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a person.”
Jesus left that place and came to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know he was there, but he could not remain hidden.
For immediately a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, and she came and fell at his feet.
The woman was a Gentile from Phoenicia in Syria. She begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
Jesus said to her, “Let the children eat their fill first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she answered him, “Yes, my Lord, even the dogs under the tables eat the children's crumbs.”
Jesus said to her, “Go. Because of what you have said, the demon has left your daughter.”
She went home and found her daughter lying on the bed, and the demon had gone out of her.
Jesus again left the region of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, in the region of the Ten Cities.
They brought him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
He took him aside, away from the crowd, put his fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.
He looked up to heaven, sighed, and said to him, “Be opened.”
Immediately his ears were opened, the bond on his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
He warned them not to tell anyone. But the more he warned them, the more they proclaimed it.
They were utterly amazed and said, “He does everything well. He makes the deaf hear and those who cannot speak, speak.”
In those days, when there was a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called his disciples and said to them,
“I have compassion for this crowd, because they have now stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away.”
His disciples said to him, “Where can anyone get enough bread here in this deserted place to feed all these people?”
He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said to him, “Seven.”
He instructed the crowds to sit down on the ground. He took those seven loaves, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served them to the crowds.
They also had a few fish. He blessed these too and said to serve them.
They ate and were satisfied, and they gathered seven baskets of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand people who ate.
He sent them away and immediately got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out and began to argue with him. They asked him for a sign from heaven, testing him.
He sighed in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation ask for a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
He left them and got into the boat, and they went to the other side.
They had forgotten to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
He warned them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
They discussed it with one another, saying, “We have no bread.”
But Jesus knew and said to them, “Why are you discussing the fact that you have no bread? Do you still not know or understand? Are your hearts still hard?
You have eyes, yet do you not see? You have ears, yet do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke those five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
He said to them, “And when I broke seven for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” They said, “Seven.”
He said to them, “How is it that you still do not understand?”
He came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
He took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat on his eyes, laid his hand on him, and asked him what he could see.
He looked and said, “I see people like trees walking around.”
Again he placed his hand on his eyes, and his sight was restored. He could see everything clearly.
He sent him home, saying, “Do not even go into the village, and do not tell anyone in the village.”
Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he questioned his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say I am?”
They said, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”
Jesus said to them, “But you, who do you say I am?” Simon answered him, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
He sternly warned them not to tell anyone about him.
He began to teach them that the Son of Man was to suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
He spoke about this openly and plainly. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Simon, saying, “Get behind me, Satan! You are not thinking about the things of God, but the things of human beings.”
Jesus called the crowds together with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake and for the sake of my good news will save it.
For what will a person gain if he gains the whole world but loses his soul?
Or what will a person give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this sinful and adulterous generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father's glory with his holy angels.
And he said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”
After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transformed before their eyes.
His clothing shone and became very white, like snow, whiter than people on earth can make it.
And Elijah and Moses appeared to them, talking with Jesus.
Peter said to him, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
But he did not know what he was saying, for they were afraid.
A cloud appeared and overshadowed them. A voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”
And suddenly, when the disciples looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, he instructed them not to tell anyone anything they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept this saying to themselves and questioned what this saying, “when he has risen from the dead,” meant.
And they asked him, “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He said to them, “Elijah comes first to set everything right. And how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer greatly and be rejected?
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”
When he came to the disciples, he saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
Immediately, the whole crowd saw him and was astonished, and they ran to greet him.
And he asked the scribes, “What are you arguing about with them?”
Someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that cannot speak.
Wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered him, “O unbelieving generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
They brought him to him. When the spirit saw him, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions, and he fell to the ground and writhed, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked his father, “How long has he been like this?” He said to him, “Since his childhood.
Many times it has thrown him into fire and water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help me and have compassion on me.”
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, everything is possible for someone who believes.”
Immediately the boy’s father cried out in tears and said, “I believe, my Lord! Help my lack of faith!”

When Jesus saw that the crowd was running and gathering around him, he rebuked the unclean spirit and said to it, “Deaf spirit that cannot speak, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!”
That demon screamed loudly, convulsed him, and came out. The boy became like a dead person, so that many said, “He is dead.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up.
When Jesus entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
He said to them, “This kind cannot come out by anything except fasting and prayer.”
After he left there, they traveled through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know about him.
For he was teaching his disciples and telling them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands. They will kill him, and after he is killed, he will rise on the third day.”
But they did not understand this statement and were afraid to ask him.
They came to Capernaum. When they entered the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing among yourselves on the road?”
But they remained silent, because on the road they had argued with one another about who was greatest among them.
Jesus sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
He took a child and stood him in their midst. Then he took him in his arms and said to them,
“Whoever welcomes a child like this in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”
John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we stopped him because he does not follow us.”
Jesus said to them, “Do not stop him, for no one who performs miracles in my name can soon afterward speak evil of me.
“Therefore, whoever is not against you is for you.”
“Whoever gives you even a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.”
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble would be better off if a donkey-driven millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
“If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go to hell,
“where their worm does not die and their fire is not extinguished.
“And if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and fall into hell,
“where their worm does not die and their fire is not extinguished.
“And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and fall into the fire of hell,
“where their worm does not die and their fire is not extinguished.
“For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
“Salt is good, but if salt loses its flavor, with what will it be salted? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
He got up and left there and came to the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Large crowds went to him there, and he taught them again, as was his custom.
The Pharisees approached him to test him and asked whether a man was permitted to divorce his wife.
He said to them, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses permitted us to write a certificate of divorce and divorce her.”
Jesus answered them, “Because of your hardness of heart, he wrote this commandment for you.”
“But from the beginning, God made them male and female.
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
and the two of them will become one flesh. So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has joined together, no human being should separate.”
His disciples asked him about this again in the house.
He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery.
And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”
People were bringing children to him so that he would touch them, but his disciples were rebuking those who brought them.
When Jesus saw this, he was displeased and said to them, “Let the children come to me, and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to those who are like these children.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.”
He took them in his arms, laid his hand on them, and blessed them.
As he was traveling along the road, a man ran up, fell to his knees, and asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not murder. Do not give false testimony. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.”
He answered him, “Teacher, I have kept all these since my youth.”

Jesus looked at him and loved him. He said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Take up the cross and come, follow me.”
But he became gloomy at these words and went away grieving, because he had many possessions.
Jesus looked at his disciples and said to them, “How difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were amazed at his words. Jesus spoke again and said to them, “My children, how difficult it is for those who trust in their wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
But they were all the more amazed and said among themselves, “Who, then, can live?”
Jesus looked at them and said to them, “For human beings this is impossible, but not for God, for everything is possible with God.”
Peter began to say, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
Jesus answered, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or villages for my sake and for the sake of my good news,
who will not receive a hundred times as much now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and villages, along with persecution—and in the age to come, eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. They were amazed and followed him in fear. He took his twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him, flog him, spit in his face, and kill him. On the third day he will rise.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.”
He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant us that one may sit at your right and one at your left in your glory.”
But he said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink and be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
They said to him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to grant, except to those for whom it has been prepared.”
When the ten heard this, they began to grumble against James and John.
Jesus called them and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
But it must not be so among you. Instead, whoever among you wants to become great must be your servant,
and whoever among you wants to be first must be everyone's slave.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
They came to Jericho. As Jesus was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, a blind man, Timaeus son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road begging.
He heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene and began to cry out, saying, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him, telling him to be quiet. But he cried out all the more, saying, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered them to call him. They called the blind man and said to him, “Take courage! Get up! He is calling you.”
The blind man threw off his cloak, got up, and came to Jesus.
Jesus said to him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabbi, let me see.”
Jesus said to him, “See! Your faith has made you well.” Immediately he could see, and he went along the road.
As he approached Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany, by the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples.
He told them, “Go to the village opposite us. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘Our Lord needs it,’ and he will send it here immediately.”
They went and found a colt tied at a doorway, outside in the street. As they were untying it,
Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
they told them what Jesus had instructed them to say, and they let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and Jesus mounted it.
Many spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
Those ahead of him and those behind him were shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
And blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything, and since it was evening, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
The next day, as he left Bethany, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree in the distance with leaves on it and went over to see whether he could find anything on it. When he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, because it was not the season for figs.
He said to it, “From now on, may no one ever eat fruit from you again.” His disciples heard him, and they came to Jerusalem.
Jesus entered the temple of God and began driving out those who were buying and selling in the temple. He overturned the money changers’ tables and the seats of those selling doves.
He would not allow anyone to carry goods through the temple.
He taught them, saying, “Is it not written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
The chief priests and the scribes heard this and were looking for a way to kill him. For they were afraid of him, because all the people were amazed at his teaching.
And when evening came, they went out of the city.
In the morning, as they passed by, they saw that the fig tree had withered from its roots.
Simon remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered.”
Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.
For truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and fall into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, will have what he says.
That is why I tell you: whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you are receiving it, and it will be yours.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your offenses.”
But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your offenses.
They came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him.
They said to him, “By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority to do these things?”
But Jesus said to them, “I too will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Where did John’s baptism come from—from heaven or from human beings? Tell me.”
They discussed it among themselves, saying, “If we tell him, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From human beings’—there is reason to fear the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.”
So they answered Jesus, “We do not know.” He said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower in it. He leased it to tenant farmers and went away.
At the proper time he sent his servant to the tenant farmers to collect some of the vineyard’s fruit.
But they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent another servant to them. They stoned this one too, wounded him, and sent him away in disgrace.
Again he sent another, and they killed this one too. He sent many other servants; some they beat, and others they killed.
Finally, he had one beloved son, and he sent him to them last, for he said, ‘Perhaps they will respect my son.’
But those tenant farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy those tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This has come from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had told this parable against them. So they left him and went away.
They sent some of the scribes and some of Herod’s followers to him to trap him in what he said.

They came and asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not concern yourself with anyone’s opinion, for you do not show favoritism, but teach the way of God truthfully. Is it lawful to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay it or not?”
But he knew their deceit and said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so I can look at it.”
They brought one to him. He said to them, “Whose image and inscription are these?” They said, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus said to them, “Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.” And they were amazed at him.
Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but leaves no children, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without leaving any children.
The second married her and died, also leaving no children. The third did the same.
All seven married her and left no children. Last of all, the woman also died.
At the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven married her.
Jesus said to them, “Isn't this why you are mistaken—because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, men do not take wives, nor do women become wives of men, but they are like the angels in heaven.
But concerning the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses how God spoke to him from the bush, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. So you are badly mistaken.”
One of the scribes came forward and heard them debating. Seeing that he had answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus said to him, “The first of all the commandments is: ‘Hear, Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher! You have truly said that he is one and that there is no other besides him.

And for a person to love him with all his heart, with all his mind, with all his soul, and with all his strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is worth more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he replied to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him anymore.
While teaching in the temple, Jesus said, “How can the scribes say that the Messiah is David's son?
For David himself said through the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool beneath your feet.’
David himself therefore calls him ‘my Lord.’ How, then, is he his son?” And the whole crowd listened to him gladly.
In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces,
the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows' houses while making a pretense of lengthy prayers. They will receive a harsher judgment.”
As Jesus sat opposite the treasury, he watched how the crowds put money into the treasury. Many rich people were putting in large amounts.
A poor widow came and put in two small coins, worth a farthing.
Jesus called his disciples and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all the others who are contributing.
For they all contributed from their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had—all she possessed.”
As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”
But Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be torn down.”
As Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
“Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign that all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
Then Jesus began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name and say, ‘I am he,’ and they will lead many astray.
When you hear of wars and reports of battles, do not be afraid. This must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and unrest. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
But watch yourselves, for they will hand you over to judges, and you will be flogged in their synagogues. You will stand before kings and governors because of me, as a testimony to them.
But first my good news must be proclaimed among all nations.

When they bring you forward to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, or rehearse it. Instead, say whatever is given to you at that time, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
You will be hated by everyone because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
But when you see the defiling sign of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Anyone on the roof must not come down or go inside to take anything from his house.
Anyone in the field must not turn back to get his clothing.
But how terrible it will be for pregnant women and those nursing children in those days!
Pray that your flight will not take place in winter.
For in those days there will be suffering unlike anything that has happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, or ever will happen.
If the Lord had not shortened those days, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones whom he chose, he shortened those days.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Messiah!’ or ‘Look, there he is!’ do not believe it.
For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders, and they will lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
But be on your guard. Look, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that suffering, the sun will grow dark, and the moon will not give its light.
The stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
Then he will send his angels and gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Now learn a lesson from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer has arrived.
So also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the door.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But about that day and that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Be watchful, stay awake, and pray, for you do not know when the time will come.
For it is like a man who went on a journey, left his house, gave authority to his servants and each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake, because you do not know when the master of the house will come—in the evening, at midnight, at the rooster’s crowing, or in the morning.
Otherwise, he may come suddenly and find you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to all of you: Stay awake.
Now the Passover of Unleavened Bread was two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they were saying, “Not during the festival, or there may be an uproar among the people.”

While he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at the table, a woman came carrying a jar of very expensive perfume made from the finest nard. She opened it and poured it over Jesus’ head.
But some of the disciples were inwardly upset and said, “Why has this perfume been wasted?
It could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they were indignant about it.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish, you can do good for them. But I am not always with you.
She has done what she could. She has perfumed my body beforehand for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this good news of mine is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.”
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
When they heard this, they were glad and promised to give him money. And he began looking for an opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Jews sacrifice the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
Wherever he enters, say to the owner of the house, ‘Our teacher says: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover meal with my disciples?’
He will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”
His disciples went out and came into the city. They found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he arrived with his twelve disciples.
While they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with me will betray me.”
They began to be distressed and said to him one by one, “Is it me?”
He said to them, “It is one of the twelve, who is dipping with me in the bowl.”
And the Son of Man goes as it is written about him. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. He said to them, “Take this; this is my body.”
He took a cup, gave thanks, blessed it, and gave it to them. They all drank from it.
He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.”
“Truly I tell you, I will not drink again from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
They sang praises and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and his sheep will be scattered.’
“But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter said to him, “Even if they all fall away, I will not.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But he insisted all the more, “Even if I have to die with you, I will not deny you, my Lord.” And they all said the same.
They came to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with him, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.
He said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
He went a little farther, fell to the ground, and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from him.
He said, “Father, my Father, you can do everything. Take this cup away from me. But not my own will, but yours.”
He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?”
“Keep watch and pray so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing and ready, but the body is weak.”
He went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
He returned again and found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy. They did not know what to say to him.
He came a third time and said to them, “Sleep now and rest. The end has arrived, and the hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.”
“Get up, let us go. Look, the one who is betraying me is approaching.”
While he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, arrived with a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
The betrayer who was handing him over had given them a signal, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him carefully and lead him away.”
He immediately approached him and said to him, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
Then they laid hands on him and arrested him.
But one of those standing there drew a sword and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his ear.
But Jesus answered them, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber?”
“Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But this happened so that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
Then his disciples abandoned him and fled.
A young man was following him, wearing only a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seized him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
They led Jesus away to Caiaphas the high priest, and all the chief priests, scribes, and elders gathered around him.
Simon followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the attendants, warming himself by the fire.
The chief priests and their whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they found none.
For although many testified against him, their testimonies did not agree.
Some stood up as false witnesses against him and said:
“We heard him say, ‘I will tear down this temple made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”
But even then their testimony did not agree.
The high priest stood up in the midst of them and questioned Jesus, saying, “Have you no answer? What is this testimony these men are giving against you?”
But he remained silent and gave him no answer. Again the high priest questioned him, saying, “Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Jesus said to him, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his tunic and said, “Why do we need witnesses anymore?
Look, you have heard the blasphemy from his own mouth. What do you think?” They all judged him deserving of death.
Some began spitting in his face, covering his face, striking him, and saying, “Prophesy!” And the guards struck him on the cheeks.
While Simon was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls came.
She saw him warming himself, looked closely at him, and said to him, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
But he denied it, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.” He went outside to the entrance, and a rooster crowed.
That servant girl saw him again and began saying to those standing there, “This man is also one of them.”
But he denied it again. A little later, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “You certainly are one of them, for you too are a Galilean, and your speech matches.”
But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
Immediately the rooster crowed for the second time. Then Simon remembered what Jesus had told him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he began to weep.
Immediately in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders, the scribes, and the whole council. They bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You have said it.”
The chief priests were accusing him of many things.
But Pilate asked him again, “Are you not going to answer? Look how much testimony they are giving against you!”
But Jesus gave no answer at all, so that Pilate was amazed.
At every festival he was accustomed to release one prisoner for them, whichever one they requested.
There was a man called Barabbas who was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the uprising.
The people shouted and began asking him to do as he usually did for them.
Pilate answered, “Do you want me to release the king of the Jews for you?”
For Pilate knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests urged the crowds all the more to have him release Barabbas for them.
Pilate said to them, “What, then, do you want me to do with this man you call the king of the Jews?”
They shouted again, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the more, “Crucify him!”
Pilate wanted to satisfy the crowds, so he released Barabbas for them. After having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to them to be crucified.
The soldiers led him inside the courtyard, that is, the Praetorium, and called together the whole cohort.
They dressed him in purple, wove a crown of thorns, and placed it on him.
They began to salute him: “Hail, king of the Jews!”
They kept striking him on the head with a reed and spitting in his face. They knelt down on their knees and bowed before him.
After mocking him, they stripped him of the purple clothing and dressed him in his own clothes. Then they led him out to crucify him.
They forced a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the village—the father of Alexander and Rufus—to carry his cross.
And they brought him to Golgotha, a place whose name means “Skull.”
They gave him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
When they had crucified him, they divided his clothes, casting lots for them to determine who would take what.
It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.
The charge for which he was put to death was written in an inscription: “This is the King of the Jews.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.
And the Scripture was fulfilled that said, “He was counted among lawbreakers.”
Those passing by also insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who tear down the temple and rebuild it in three days,
save yourself and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests and the scribes mocked him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself!
Let the Messiah, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so that we may see and believe in him!” Even those crucified with him were insulting him.
At noon, darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon.
At three in the afternoon, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “El, El, why have you abandoned me?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some of those standing there who heard him said, “He is calling Elijah.”
Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, and fastened it to a reed to give him a drink. They said, “Wait! Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
But Jesus cried out with a loud voice and died.
The curtain at the entrance to the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing near him saw that he cried out and died in this way, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
There were also women watching from a distance: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
These women had followed him and served him when he was in Galilee. There were also many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And when Friday evening came, which is before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected member of the council who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God. He took courage, went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
Pilate was surprised that he was already dead. He summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had been dead for some time.
When he learned that he had, he gave his body to Joseph.
Joseph bought linen, took him down, and wrapped him in it. He laid him in a tomb that had been cut into the rock and rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could go and anoint him.
Early in the morning on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb as the sun rose.
They were saying to one another, “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?”
When they looked, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
They entered the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were astonished.
But he said to them, “Do not be afraid. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here. Look, here is the place where he was laid.”
But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.’
When they heard, they fled and came out of the tomb, for amazement and trembling had seized them. They said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
Early on the first day of the week, he rose and appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went and brought the news to those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
When they heard the women saying that he was alive and had appeared to them, they did not believe them.
After this, he appeared in a different form to two of them as they were walking and going to a village.
They went and told the rest, but they did not believe them either.

Finally, he appeared to the eleven as they were reclining at a meal. He rebuked them for their lack of faith and their hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him after he had risen.
He said to them, ‘Go into all the world and proclaim my good news throughout all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons, and they will speak in new languages.
They will pick up snakes, and if they drink deadly poison, it will not harm them. They will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.’
After our Lord Jesus had spoken with them, he went up to heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
They went out and proclaimed the message everywhere. Our Lord helped them and confirmed their words through the signs they performed.
